messages:
incident-bot: Pager — P0: Multi-node tensor/pipeline job experiencing repeated communicator resets and hangs; multiple inference workers failing. cluster=redwood-prod, affected_pool=gpupool-12x, impact=high. Runbook: /runbooks/multi-gpu-comm.md
alyssa.dev: i'm oncall, taking this. seeing a lot of `NCCL WARN` followed by kernel launch errors, jobs stuck in 'waiting for rendezvous'
pranav.s: logs from gpuprod-45 show `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` + kernel watchdog timeouts. dmesg: "GPU fault: code 0x50 at ffff..."
tess_ops: cs ping — Orchid Health reporting 500s on model inference. @cs-acctmgr any customer-visible error rate numbers?
cs-acctmgr: Orchid Health: ~12% of requests 500s last 10m, they have low retry logic so backend errors are surfacing. notified account team.
miguel_infra: i can cordon gpuprod-45 and drain, but that will evict running jobs (they'll restart elsewhere). alternative: try forcing intra-node routing for affected models to avoid cross-node collectives
alyssa.dev: agree. for now we'll try policy change + env tweaks for canary before mass cordon. plan: 1) canary env: NCCL_TIMEOUT=300, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO 2) route traffic prefer_local_gpu=true 3) monitor errors for 15m
chris_oncall: quick note: we've seen intermittent IB flakiness cause exactly this pattern. increasing NCCL_TIMEOUT only mitigates, disabling IB forces TCP and is more stable for cross-node on flaky fabric
alyssa.dev: applying canary env to model-serve deployment now
---
Command run:
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-serve NCCL_TIMEOUT=300 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO --record
---
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for model-serve canary (2/5 pods updated)
alyssa.dev: tailing logs from canary pod: repeating loop: `nccl_comm.c:142 NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank returned internal error` then `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` -> hang
pranav.s: trying a quick repro with NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 + NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to force TCP only. if that stabilizes, we can push cluster-wide until infra can investigate IB fabric
miguel_infra: spun a short test job with NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 + NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for same model; it completed warmup and ran 10 minutes stable (previously failed in ~2m).
cs-acctmgr: Orchid Health error rate down to ~3% after canary env applied, but still some 500s. they're asking for ETA to safe rollback or permanent fix
tess_ops: if canary stays green for 15m we can roll change to primary. rollback option: revert to previous image which will drop throughput ~30% — will that be acceptable?
alyssa.dev: prefer to continue canary. if errors plateau <1% we keep change. i'll also cordon gpuprod-45 if it keeps flapping.
chris_oncall: note for postmortem: check HCA firmware and switch counters for gpuprod-45, and NCCL debug logs (set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`) — capture before next restart
alyssa.dev: handing off to night oncall @pranav.s for follow-up and full handoff notes. current status: canary partially rolled (2/5), errors reduced from ~18/min to ~1/min, customers affected: Orchid Health (partial), Beta test group (minor). leaving runbook links below
pranav.s: taking over. will continue canary to full rollout if stable. will schedule maintenance to repro with IB enabled and collect NIC/switch counters. next steps I will take:
```
- monitor canary for 30m
- if stable, roll to production (all pods) with same envs
- cordon gpuprod-45 and collect full `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,BOARD,REASON` and `ibstat` logs from node
- open infra ticket to validate HCA firmware and switch port errors
- if IB suspected, plan controlled rollback to TCP-only until fabric is fixed
```

pranav.s: leaving handoff note for morning crew. :white_check_mark:  
alyssa.dev: thanks — adding reaction :thumbsup: and posting to incident tracker 1826574321 in incidents.
incidents-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042, severity=P0, owner=pranav.s, slack-thread=1826574321
pranav.s: will also follow up with CS to confirm Orchid Health post-mitigation state.
cs-acctmgr: noted, i'll update the customer and set expectation for a follow-up in 2 hours. :telephone_receiver:
